InitialDescription: Gentle and clean. Fine particles release a soft rice aroma; it does not suit excessive force or overlong grinding.
Carries light bitterness and sweet return. Fast grinding releases bitterness first, so it suits slow handling.
Rich and deep, useful as a main note or tail note. Too much or too heavy processing can make it bitter and dominant.
Mild and smooth. It supports body and sticky texture, but usually should not lead the aroma.
Solid and warm. It gives a biscuit-like nut aroma and blends well with similar nutty ingredients.
Thick and warm. It is suited to building a base aroma before lighter notes appear.
Bright and slightly bitter. It works well as a middle or finishing lift, but can become bitter if handled too early or too much.
Clean and mild. It rounds the finish and should not take the lead too early.
Deep, dry, and aromatic. It needs stronger pressure to open, but excessive force turns it harsh.
A support ingredient. It should stay low in ratio and should not become the main aroma.
Clear and piercing. Medium speed opens it without making it rush out harshly.
Light and fragile. It should appear late and in low proportion, supported by mild grain aroma.
Savory and fermented. Medium force opens the body; too much pressure makes it dull, bitter, or muddy.
Fresh and sharp. Medium speed and middle order help it blend into the main body without rushing forward.
Fresh and watery. It should be handled lightly and late so its green finish is not buried.
